Fresh checks of Tsuyoshi Yamamoto, Jazz House ALFIE, BODY&SOUL, Space M&A, current schedule traces, and credible Japanese-jazz sources did not reveal a new verified future Yamamoto appearance not already represented in canonical/curated/processed intake. The broader US-corridor pass found Niladri Kumaar at Sixth & I in Washington, DC on October 24. Stage 1 admits the specific performance because The Space Between the Notes is built around Kumaar's musical dialogue with the late Zakir Hussain and repertoire connected to their only documented full live performance, recast for sitar/zitar, tabla, keys, and drums; the memorial, instrumental, and improvisational context is concrete to this project rather than fame or venue prestige. Stage 2 assigns A+. This is an excellent local performance worth actively making room for, but the same project is a multi-city 2026-2027 tour, so there is no verified scarcity fact that supports protect-the-night or alter-plans urgency. The current/recent RADAR distribution was sanity-checked against the durable rubric before finalizing the grade; this pass adds no S or S+ event. Repository searches for the exact stable event ID and exact Sixth & I billing returned no existing canonical, curated, or processed representation before publication. The original May 2026 Washington Performing Arts season announcement listed Charlie Lindner on keys and Dèmitrio Albano on drums, while the current exact Washington Performing Arts and Sixth & I event pages now agree on Agnelo Fernandes on keys and Sambit Chatterjee on drums; the current exact event pages govern the published lineup.

events.category: Hindustani classical / Sitar / Zakir Hussain tribute
events.factual_description: Washington Performing Arts presents Niladri Kumaar at Sixth & I in Washington, DC on Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 7:30 PM, with doors at 6:30 PM. The current Sixth & I and Washington Performing Arts event pages list Niladri Kumaar on sitar, Agnelo Fernandes on keys, Sambit Chatterjee on drums, and Satyajit Talwalkar on tabla, with the program titled The Space Between the Notes. The presenters describe the program as a forward-looking showcase and tribute to Kumaar's musical bond with the late Zakir Hussain, drawing on their only documented full live performance and expanding the music through sitar, zitar, tabla, keys, drums, and jazz-influenced improvisation. Sixth & I lists $50 admission; the authorized Washington Performing Arts ticket page shows $50 face value plus $9 fees and currently marks the event sold out. Apple Music lists Space Between the Notes by Zakir Hussain and Niladri Kumar as a three-track Hindustani classical album released August 14, 2026.

enrichment.note: Exact Washington Performing Arts event and ticket destinations are verified, and Apple Music now carries the exact Space Between the Notes album released August 14, 2026. The current ticket page is marked sold out. Current exact event pages supersede the older season-announcement personnel listing.

en.why_it_matters: Kumaar is not simply bringing a sitar recital to Washington: he is carrying repertoire shaped by his long musical dialogue with Zakir Hussain into a new ensemble of tabla, keys, and drums. Because the project grows out of the duo's only documented full live performance, the memorial context and the instrument's improvisational voice are part of the music itself rather than a promotional frame.
en.trip_verdict: For a DMV night, actively make room if a ticket surfaces; the official ticket page is currently sold out. There is no reason to travel up the corridor for another stop when this substantial version of the project is landing locally.
en.listen_before: Zakir Hussain & Niladri Kumar — Space Between the Notes

es.why_it_matters: Kumaar no viene simplemente a dar un recital de sitar en Washington: trae repertorio formado por su larga conversación musical con Zakir Hussain y lo lleva a un nuevo ensamble de tabla, teclados y batería. Como el proyecto nace de la única interpretación completa en vivo documentada del dúo, el contexto de homenaje y la voz improvisatoria del instrumento forman parte de la música misma, no sólo del discurso promocional.
es.trip_verdict: Para una noche en el DMV sí le haría espacio activamente si aparece un boleto; la venta oficial figura actualmente agotada. No hay razón para subir por el corredor a perseguir otra parada cuando esta versión sustancial del proyecto llega directamente a Washington.
